term_glossary.plain_words: Infinitesimal change in the sample x_t along a forward trajectory.
Diffusion coefficient g(t) = sqrt(2t) injecting Brownian noise dw_t.
Exact marginal probability density surface over (x, t).

formulas.derivation_or_motivation: Under the Karras/VE schedule sigma(t) = t with zero drift f(x,t) = 0 and g(t) = sqrt(2t), the Itô integral from 0 to t adds Gaussian variance int_0^t 2s ds = t^2. Convolving the bimodal prior p_0(x) (modes at +/- mu_0 = +/- 2.0, width sigma_0 = 0.35) with N(0, t^2) yields the exact closed-form marginal density p_t(x) with variance v(t) = sigma_0^2 + t^2.
formulas.common_misreading: Thinking the marginal p_t(x) requires simulating thousands of paths; for Gaussian perturbations, p_t(x) is known analytically at every time t.

term_glossary.plain_words: The score vector field: spatial gradient of log probability density.
Exact bimodal score: tanh selects the nearer mode +/- mu_0 and pulls x toward it.
Tweedie's MMSE denoiser E[x_0 | x_t] recovered directly from the score.

formulas.derivation_or_motivation: Writing p_t(x) = (2 pi v(t))^(-1/2) exp(-(x^2 + mu_0^2)/(2 v(t))) cosh(mu_0 x / v(t)) with v(t) = sigma_0^2 + t^2 and differentiating log p_t(x) with respect to x gives (mu_0 tanh(mu_0 x / v(t)) - x) / v(t). At x = 0, tanh(0) = 0 so the score vanishes along the watershed.
formulas.common_misreading: Assuming the score points straight to the origin x = 0; for t < sqrt(mu_0^2 - sigma_0^2) = 1.969, x = 0 is a local minimum valley and the score points outward toward +/- mu_0.

term_glossary.plain_words: Deterministic velocity of a trajectory moving through space-time.
Half the squared diffusion coefficient (1/2 * 2t = t) replaces stochastic noise.
Clean deterministic Probability Flow ODE velocity under the Karras schedule.

formulas.derivation_or_motivation: In the Fokker-Planck equation d_t p_t = -div(f p_t) + 0.5 g(t)^2 Lap(p_t), rewriting Lap(p_t) = div(p_t grad_x log p_t) turns the PDE into a pure continuity equation d_t p_t = -div([f - 0.5 g(t)^2 grad_x log p_t] p_t). Thus the deterministic ODE dx/dt = f(x,t) - 0.5 g(t)^2 grad_x log p_t(x) has the exact same marginal density p_t(x) at every t as the stochastic SDE.
formulas.common_misreading: Believing removing noise changes the marginal distribution p_t(x); the factor 1/2 in the score coefficient exactly compensates for the removed Brownian diffusion.

term_glossary.plain_words: Consistency map evaluated at a high-noise point (x_t, t) on an ODE trajectory.
Consistency map at any other time t' along the same Probability Flow ODE trajectory.
The unique clean endpoint on the data manifold t = epsilon.

formulas.derivation_or_motivation: Song, Dhariwal, Chen, & Sutskever (OpenAI, 2023) define the consistency function f: (x_t, t) -> x_epsilon as the backward flow map of the Probability Flow ODE. Any two points (x_t, t) and (x_{t'}, t') lying on the same ODE solution curve must map to the identical endpoint x_epsilon.
formulas.common_misreading: Confusing a consistency model with a single-step Euler approximation x - t dx/dt; a true consistency model integrates the curved ODE streamline all the way to t = epsilon in one evaluation.

term_glossary.plain_words: Skip connection weight c_skip(t) that approaches 1 as t -> epsilon.
Network output weight c_out(t) that vanishes at t = epsilon so f_theta(x, epsilon) = x holds identically.

formulas.derivation_or_motivation: Following Karras et al. (2022) and Song et al. (2023), parametrizing f_theta(x, t) with differentiable coefficients c_skip(t) and c_out(t) guarantees the boundary condition f_theta(x, epsilon) = x without penalty terms because c_skip(epsilon) = 1 and c_out(epsilon) = 0 exactly.
formulas.common_misreading: Treating f_theta(x, epsilon) = x as a soft loss term; in Consistency Models it is enforced architecturally via c_skip and c_out.

checks.description: Verify score at watershed x=0 is identically zero for all t
Verify bifurcation time t* = sqrt(mu_0^2 - sigma_0^2) where x=0 transitions from valley to peak
Verify boundary condition c_skip(epsilon) == 1.0 and c_out(epsilon) == 0.0

sources: Song et al. (2021), Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations, ICLR 2021.
Song, Dhariwal, Chen, & Sutskever (2023), Consistency Models, ICML 2023 (OpenAI).
Karras, Aittala, Aila, & Laine (2022), Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models, NeurIPS 2022.
